neighbours.label: a clause-final hedge that limits or denies the whole claim ('if ... at all', 'and never will')
fire: The old bridge will be repaired slowly, if it is repaired at all.
Tickets are hard to get these days, if you can get them at all.
The senator rarely answers questions from reporters, if she answers at all.
The river freezes only briefly in this region, if it freezes at all.
He has never apologized for the remark, and he never will.
That shop has never offered a discount, and it never will.
The rule applies to very few cases, if it applies at all.
My brother has never liked olives, and I doubt he ever will.
quiet: The old bridge will be repaired slowly over the next two summers.
Tickets are hard to get these days, so we booked them in March.
The senator rarely answers questions from reporters after the session.
The river freezes only briefly in this region during January.
He has apologized for the remark, and the matter is now closed.
That shop has offered a discount every spring since it opened.
The rule applies to most cases involving rented property.
My brother has liked olives since he was a little boy.

predictions: 'at all' in 'if X at all' and the closing 'will' of 'never has ... and never will' fire; the same sentences ending without the hedge stay quiet.
notes: Probe: 'if it recovered at all' 0.779, 'if you can find it at all' 0.652, 'and he never will' 0.462, 'unintentionally' 0.462, 'as the records allow' 0.326; 'open all week' 0.010, plain clause 0.015.
